items.author: Contributor 01
items.body: I compared the March interval export with the controller event log. The largest peaks line up with overlapping defrost starts, not ordinary cooling load. I can test a stagger before we discuss equipment changes.
items.title: Initial overlap finding

items.author: Contributor 01
items.body: Could you sanity-check how the older controller reports local timestamps? My parser currently treats the export as site-local time with an explicit offset.
items.title: Timestamp check request

items.author: Contributor 04
items.body: Night one completed. We followed three recommendations and held one because a pallet inspection kept a door open. No temperature alarms. The handover line was useful.
items.title: First trial night

items.author: Contributor 02
items.body: Nice work by Contributor 01 getting the peak down 38 kW.
items.title: Informal praise

items.author: Contributor 01
items.body: Do we have enough to call the pilot a saving in the quarterly note? I would describe only the observed 38 kW peak difference and the unchanged energy reading.
items.title: Quarterly wording question

items.author: Contributor 01
items.body: Working hypothesis: separate eligible defrost starts by 12 minutes while preserving temperature and maximum-delay limits. Compare peak demand, energy, alarms, door-open periods, and product-temperature excursions. This is a proposal, not an approved control change.
items.title: Staggering hypothesis

items.author: Contributor 01
items.body: Draft trial: Freezer B only, 01:00–05:00, six nights. Scheduler proposes starts; operator confirms them. Stop on temperature alarm, missed defrost, controller rejection, or operator concern. Baseline excludes the ambiguous clock-change interval.
items.title: Pilot plan draft

items.author: Contributor 08
items.body: Meter result for the four Freezer B trial windows: highest 15-minute demand was 38 kW below the matched baseline maximum. Total energy differed by less than meter resolution. Door-open time was also lower on two trial nights, so the peak change cannot be assigned wholly to staggering.
items.title: Freezer B meter result

items.author: Contributor 01
items.body: Documented recommendation-mode startup, operator hold, rejection handling, audit export, rollback, and the distinction between supported Freezer B controllers and unsupported R4 gateways. Drafted from the pilot handovers.
items.title: Operating guide

items.author: Contributor 01
items.body: Added event-log parser, overlap detector, and a small simulator for candidate start offsets. Output includes original and proposed coincidence counts; no controller-writing path.
items.title: Initial analysis tooling

items.author: Contributor 02
items.body: Lantern remains a supervised practice at Freezer B. The team observed a lower trial-window peak without measurable energy change; causality and tariff impact remain uncertain. Chiller C produced only two manual nights, and broader rollout awaits gateway support and more varied operating data.
items.title: Quarterly status

items.author: Contributor 07
items.body: Clock-change fixture produces two events with the same normalized instant. The parser assumes an offset that is absent from the source file, so the March overlap count is inflated by one event.
items.title: DST normalization defect

items.author: Contributor 01
items.body: Parser now preserves ambiguous local times, excludes unresolved events from matched comparisons, and reports the excluded count. Added Contributor 07's duplicated-hour fixture and six ordinary-day cases.
items.title: Timestamp handling correction

items.author: Contributor 01
items.body: Added read-only schedule recommendations, 12-minute separation, temperature eligibility checks, maximum-delay display, audit logging, and operator hold. No automatic command submission.
items.title: Recommendation-mode implementation

items.author: Contributor 05
items.body: East-site gateway rejects proposed-delay metadata on controller revision R4. Need either a vendor-supported mapping or a site-specific adapter. This blocks the planned screen-assisted workflow, not manual operations.
items.title: R4 gateway incompatibility

items.author: Contributor 07
items.body: During a bench test, losing the telemetry stream leaves the last recommendation visible for up to five minutes. It is labelled with its timestamp, but stale advice should be hidden immediately.
items.title: Stale recommendation display

items.author: Contributor 01
items.body: Hide recommendations after 30 seconds without telemetry, show a disconnected state, and require a fresh eligibility calculation after reconnect. Added stream-loss tests.
items.title: Telemetry-loss safeguard

items.author: Contributor 06
items.body: That fits the night-shift notes, although open dock doors could explain part of the same interval. Please keep both possibilities in the analysis.
items.title: Alternative explanation

items.author: Contributor 07
items.body: The spring export has no offset at all. Most days look local, but the clock-change hour is duplicated. Don't rely on the label; I will send a test fixture.
items.title: Clock-change warning

items.author: Contributor 01
items.body: Thanks, though that number is the difference between two observed maxima, not a controlled saving. Contributor 04 ran the shifts, Contributor 07 caught the time issue, and Contributor 03 set the safety constraints.
items.title: Qualification and attribution

items.author: Contributor 08
items.body: Agreed. Avoid annualising it. Tariff benefit depends on whether the trial window would otherwise have set the billing peak, which we do not know from four nights.
items.title: No annualisation

items.author: Contributor 03
items.body: Approval conditions: operations chooses trial windows; controls engineering reviews commands; safety limits remain in the controller; automatic rollback after two missed cycles or any high-temperature alarm.
items.title: Approval conditions

items.author: Contributor 04
items.body: Operations can staff four nights, not six. Add a visible hold button and a handover line saying which unit is delayed. Night supervisors own the final go/no-go each shift.
items.title: Operations revision

items.author: Contributor 04
items.body: Added shift screenshots and changed 'approve' to 'confirm recommendation'; operators are confirming a suggestion, not authorising an autonomous control action.
items.title: Operations edits

items.author: Contributor 07
items.body: Fixture passes and the corrected March result still shows repeated overlap outside the clock-change hour. Approved. This validates the analysis path, not deployment behavior.
items.title: Analysis review approval

items.author: Contributor 06
items.body: No product-temperature excursion or missed defrost was recorded. Four nights are too few for seasonal claims, and operator confirmation means this did not test unattended scheduling.
items.title: Pilot limitations

items.author: Contributor 03
items.body: Safety checks match the plan. Please make controller rejection a hard stop rather than retrying, and clarify that the maximum-delay value comes from the controller profile.
items.title: Safety review

items.author: Contributor 01
items.body: Changed rejection handling to stop and alert; labelled the profile-derived limit in the operator view. Added tests for both paths.
items.title: Review changes

items.author: Contributor 01
items.body: I can build an adapter, but without a documented field contract we could silently apply the wrong units. Recommend recording manual decisions while Contributor 05 seeks vendor confirmation.
items.title: Adapter risk assessment

items.author: Contributor 05
items.body: Vendor documentation finally confirms the R4 field uses whole minutes. Adapter work could resume, but the East-site controller replacement is now under review, so the site has not prioritised deployment.
items.title: Gateway clarification without deployment

items.author: Contributor 03
items.body: Approved after bench verification. This closes the display hazard; it does not resolve the R4 gateway incompatibility.
items.title: Safeguard approval
